name: TeamStarWolf - HTB Technique Frequency
description: Curated practitioner view, not an official MITRE mapping. Supplied aggregate of 249 analyzed HTB machines and 135 distinct techniques; derived metadata only, not reproduced walkthrough content. The original 131-machine cohort used a careful analysis pass; the additional 118 machines use coarser keyword-derived tagging over selected common techniques, which can miss rarer behaviors and produce false positives. These methods are not equally sensitive. Scores normalize counts to the maximum (209 machines), not to the sample size; 100 does not mean 100% of machines. This reflects HTB teaching and sample-selection bias, not real-world enterprise prevalence. Counts reconcile with supplied cohort metadata but were not independently re-audited against walkthroughs. IDs and tactic assignments are validated against the bundled ATT&CK v16 enterprise dataset.

legendItems.label: 100: maximum supplied count (209 of 249 machines), not 100% prevalence

metadata.name: source
metadata.value: Supplied combined HTB aggregate; source documents and machine-level metadata are not included.

metadata.name: score_meaning
metadata.value: Relative supplied count normalized to the maximum; not percentage of machines, severity, enterprise prevalence, confidence, or control coverage.

metadata.name: counting_policy
metadata.value: Counts reconcile with the original aggregate plus the additional per-machine tags. Parent and subtechnique counts remain separate supplied observations, not rolled up. Techniques overlap within machines; counts and scores are not additive.

metadata.name: tactic_policy
metadata.value: Each technique is displayed under all of its bundled ATT&CK v16 tactics with the same count and score. This is display expansion, not evidence of behavior in every tactic. Do not sum repeated tactic rows.

metadata.name: limitations
metadata.value: The original 131-machine cohort used a careful analysis pass; the additional 118 machines use coarser keyword-derived tagging over selected common techniques, which can miss rarer behaviors and produce false positives. These methods are not equally sensitive. HTB teaching and sample-selection bias limit generalization. Untagged behaviors are unmeasured, not confirmed absent. Writeups and machine identities across cohorts were not independently re-audited; validation checks supplied arithmetic and identifiers, not underlying behavioral evidence.
